chunk_findings.detail: The `env_refs_in_project_config` fact under `[harness.opencode]` omits the `v` field that this file’s own header declares for every fact (“Facts are the shared record (value, status, source, date)”) and that the same key provides under `[harness.kilo]`. A consumer that loads this file and accesses `env_refs_in_project_config["v"]` will get a `KeyError` for opencode harness facts, so opencode route resolution can fail on this shipped data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/routes/harness-provider.toml:24

chunk_findings.detail: The Jinja context built in `render` does not include `ep.streaming`, even though streaming support is one of the endpoint facts resolved and stored in `Endpoint`. The provider block for opencode/kilo is required to render that fact, but the template receives only `tool_call`, `window`, and `max_output`. A concrete failure: an endpoint with `Endpoint(..., streaming=True)` either makes `render` raise `UndefinedError` if the template references `streaming` under `StrictUndefined`, or silently omits streaming from the emitted provider block. Either way the resolved streaming fact is not rendered.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/endpoint.py:render

chunk_findings.detail: `v = ((row or {}).get("endpoint") or {}).get("v")` assumes the `endpoint` field is a dict or a falsy value. A local `.ddflow/local/models.toml` route such as `endpoint = "http://localhost:11434/v1"` is a truthy string, so this line evaluates `"http://...".get("v")` and raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'`. The function explicitly advertises returning an `unavailable` Result “or what is wrong with it,” but malformed local config crashes the launcher instead of reporting the route as unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/endpoint.py:_route_basics

chunk_findings.detail: `os.open(target, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)` only applies mode `0600` when the file is first created. If `target` already exists with `0644` or `0666`, the write truncates and replaces the file but leaves its old, more-permissive mode. The function’s contract says the private provider block is written `0600`, so this can persist a more-world-readable provider block under the lane home after an existing file exists.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/endpoint.py:write_private

chunk_findings.detail: The limit output expression `{{ max_output or window }}` falls back to the full context window when `max_output` is missing, `None`, or `0` (the code's own falsiness check). For an endpoint route with `window=128000` and no `max_output`, the rendered provider JSON contains `"limit": {"context": 128000, "output": 128000}`. This is wrong: OpenAI-compatible APIs reject `max_tokens` equal to the context window because it exceeds the model's maximum output and must be less than context minus prompt tokens. The lane endpoint then fails on every generation. The fallback should use a safe output default or omit the `output` field when `max_output` is not provided.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/harness/opencode/provider.json.j2:12

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `stat.S_IMODE(p.stat().st_mode) == 0o600` assumes POSIX permission bits. On Windows, Python reports a normal writable file as `0o666` (or `0o444`), so this test fails on a Windows runner even when `E.write_private` creates the private config correctly. The test is not marked `@pytest.mark.skipif(os.name != "posix", ...)`, and the intended portability of ddflow makes this an environment-dependent test failure.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_endpoint.py::test_verified_route_renders_for_both_harnesses

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `assert "LAN_ENDPOINT_KEY" not in repr(ep2) or "key_env" in repr(ep2)` cannot detect a leak of the actual API key value. If `repr(ep2)` is, for example, `Endpoint(api_key= [REDACTED] base_url='http://ENDPOINT-HOST')`, the first disjunct is true because the secret does not contain the env-var name, so the test passes even though the endpoint is no longer storing the key by env name only. The assertion should check for the secret value or assert that only an env-name field is present, not merely that the literal `LAN_ENDPOINT_KEY` is absent unless `key_env` appears.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_endpoint.py::test_key_by_name_only_and_keyless

chunk_findings.detail: The `[harness.opencode].env_refs_in_project_config` fact omits the `v` key even though the file header defines facts as the shared record `(value, status, source, date)` and every other fact in the file includes `v`. A consumer that materializes or validates shipped facts according to that contract (for example `Fact(**data["harness"]["opencode"]["env_refs_in_project_config"])` or `data["harness"]["opencode"]["env_refs_in_project_config"]["v"]`) fails on the shipped file; a consumer that uses `.get("v")` silently has no value for this fact. The fact should either carry an explicit value or the stated fact contract should allow unknown facts, but as written the data is inconsistent with its own schema.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/models/routes/harness-provider.toml:24

chunk_findings.detail: The `base_url` check only rejects credentials in the userinfo before the first slash. Because `re.match` with the pattern `^https?://[^/@\s]+(/|$)` is not a full-string validator, once it matches the slash it accepts any trailing characters unchecked; if there is no slash, characters such as `?` and `#` are accepted as part of the host. Given an endpoint row with `kind = "openai"`, `base_url = "https://api.deepseek.com/v1?api_key= [REDACTED] `api_key_env = ""`, and a model id, `_route_basics` returns the URL and `resolve` returns an `Endpoint`; `render` then writes the credential-bearing URL into the lane provider config. This violates the intent that keys travel by environment-variable name only and no key value is stored in endpoint data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/endpoint.py:84

chunk_findings.detail: `write_private` documents writing the provider block `0600`, but `os.open(..., 0o600)` applies the mode only when creating a new file. If the target already exists with a looser mode, e.g. `<home>/.config/opencode/opencode.json` was pre-created with mode `0644`, this call truncates and overwrites the file while leaving it group/world-readable, exposing the endpoint address. The function should explicitly enforce the mode after opening, e.g. `os.fchmod(fd, 0o600)`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/endpoint.py:156

chunk_findings.detail:
`_ENV_NAME` uses `re.match` with `^...$`, but Python `$` also matches immediately before a trailing newline. A route with `api_key_env = "DDFLOW_KEY
"` therefore passes validation, and `launch_env` returns `{ "DDFLOW_KEY
": "DDFLOW_KEY
" }`; the template can also emit `{env:DDFLOW_KEY
}`. Environment-variable names must not contain a newline, so the validator should use `re.fullmatch` or `\Z` instead of `$`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/endpoint.py:29

chunk_findings.detail: The test suite requires a usable opencode provider block to be rendered even though the opencode custom-provider family is explicitly marked unqualified. `test_unknown_route_and_harness` asserts `E.layout("opencode")["custom_provider"]["s"] == "unverified"`, while `test_verified_route_renders_for_both_harnesses` takes the default example, flips only the route-level `s = "unverified"` strings to `"verified"`, and then requires `E.write_private(ep, "opencode", home)` to return a path and a JSON config with `tool_call: true`. For input `harness="opencode"` with no probe, this renders/accepts an opencode custom-provider configuration despite the required opencode falsifier/probe not having qualified that family, contrary to “probed before use” and “a failed probe records the family unqualified”.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_endpoint.py:test_verified_route_renders_for_both_harnesses

chunk_findings.detail: The new harness-support gate checks only the fact status (`support.get("s")`) and ignores the fact value (`support.get("v")`). The project fact convention is `(value, status, source, date)`, so a harness can have a verified/documented record that custom-provider support is false, e.g. `custom_provider = {v = false, s = "verified", src = "opencode --version", d = "2026-10-31"}`. With that data, `support.get("s")` is in `facts.READABLE`, so `prepare` does not return `unavailable`; it proceeds to render and write a lane-private provider block for a harness that has been recorded as not accepting one. The gate should require `support.get("v")` truthy in addition to a readable status.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/endpoint.py:prepare

chunk_findings.detail: The new assertion only checks that the environment-variable name appears in `repr(ep2)`. It still does not detect the original leak case: if `Endpoint` also carries the resolved secret (for example `api_key= [REDACTED] while keeping `key_env='LAN_ENDPOINT_KEY'`, the assertion passes, and the host assertion also passes. The test never sets a sentinel value for `LAN_ENDPOINT_KEY` or asserts that that value is absent from `repr(ep2)` or the rendered config, so a regression that stores the actual key value instead of only the env name would still pass `test_key_by_name_only_and_keyless`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_endpoint.py:68
